reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: src/lesskey_parse.rs initializes caller-supplied command/edit/variable xbuffer descriptors and points currtable at a field inside that caller object. File parsing separately owns a saved path and an optional opened stream.
owner_creation.invariant: The table descriptor must outlive its interior currtable pointer.
limitations: Copying the aggregate does not rebase its internal pointer automatically.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/lesskey_parse.rs borrows input content and fills bounded stack line arrays before passing them to parse_line. Returned table buffers remain outside those stack arrays and must be retained or released by the caller.
aliases_escapes.invariant: No stack line address may become a persistent published table owner.
limitations: The raw tables argument still requires a valid writable aggregate.

callback_targets.analysis: src/lesskey_parse.rs calls local parse_line and xbuffer helpers directly; parse_lesskey reads native FILE data synchronously and has no stored runtime callback selector.
callback_targets.invariant: Parser callees must copy any stack line bytes they retain.
limitations: Direct calls do not establish safe reuse of an already live table descriptor.

invalidation.analysis: src/lesskey_parse.rs init_tables resets each xbuffer pointer rather than releasing an old live buffer. The current decode caller supplies a fresh staging aggregate and explicitly transfers/releases buffers, repairing M0-LEAK-003.
invalidation.invariant: Reuse requires prior owner retirement before descriptor reset.
limitations: The parser API itself remains raw and does not enforce freshness by type.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/lesskey_parse.rs appends parsed lines into caller tables while mutating global errors/linenum. Publication into active table lists occurs in decode only after the parser returns successfully.
mutation_commit.invariant: Staged parse buffers must not become active tables before parse success.
limitations: This file does not own the whole configuration publication transaction.

release_pair.analysis: src/lesskey_parse.rs closes only an opened non-stdin FILE, frees its saved lesskey_file and nulls that global. Table buffers are intentionally returned to the staging caller, whose failure path deinitializes them.
release_pair.invariant: Borrowed stdin must not take the opened-stream fclose path.
limitations: Normal file/path release is separate from returned table-buffer ownership.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/lesskey_parse.rs can return an injected parser failure after earlier lines appended data; decode then deinitializes all three unpublished buffers. Missing file-name allocation returns before init, relying on the fresh zeroed caller descriptor.
error_cleanup.invariant: Rollback must release only this parse attempt and not prior published data.
limitations: No independent parser campaign is rerun in this review.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/lesskey_parse.rs global lesskey_file/errors/linenum and the raw currtable cursor assume ordinary serialized parsing. The file registers no signal handoff; M0-MEM-001 remains open for aggregate/caller lifetime rules.
signals_handoff.invariant: Concurrent or reentrant parses must not share mutable parser globals.
limitations: No concrete handler-to-parser route is established by these definitions.

src/decode.rs.relationship: lesskey_text at src/decode.rs:2921-2958 supplies fresh staging descriptors; src/decode.rs:2970-2991 releases failed buffers and transfers successful ones, bounding the parser caller-lifetime contract.
